To protect your $1.1M commercial cleaning business from impending client churn, you must diversify away from dependence on a single property-management firm. 

The best immediate course of action is Option B: hiring a full-time outbound sales representative, supplemented by a targeted referral initiative. Option A's digital agency math yields roughly 4 to 5 contracts monthly at an unsustainable $1,800 to $2,250 acquisition cost against a $48,000 lifetime value. Option C relies too heavily on organic pacing and lacks the predictable velocity needed within your tight six-month window. 

Option B offers direct control. At $5,500 monthly, your rep targets local property managers and facility directors. Three weekly walkthroughs translate to about twelve monthly. Closing 30 percent yields roughly 3.6 new contracts monthly, replacing your current inflow at an acceptable customer acquisition cost. Utilize your operations manager to support this rep with technical scoping and walkthrough estimates.

Step one is hiring and onboarding the sales rep within thirty days, supplying them with a targeted list of mid-market commercial buildings. Step two is launching a referral network with non-competing vendors like HVAC and security contractors, offering a cash bounty for warm introductions. 

Over the next six months, the timeline is clear. Months one and two focus on outbound pipeline building and referral partnership outreach. Months three and four evaluate the rep's conversion metrics, adjusting scripts and building lists. Months five and six stabilize lead flow, ensuring you backfill any lost revenue before the acquisition fallout hits your bottom line.

This plan assumes the rep hits performance benchmarks and your operational capacity remains steady. If lead conversion drops below 20 percent by month three, pivot immediately by reallocating budget toward a hybrid digital model.
